summary.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.
summary.overview: First earnings call after the 16 September 2026 listing. Revenue from operations was INR433.6 crores (up 35.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 20.8% and PAT of INR61 crores (14.1% margin). Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

segments.name: Acetone-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; about 43% of FY26 revenue per management.

segments.name: Phosphorus-based specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: About 40% of Q1 FY27 revenue; described as the fastest-growing category, about 38% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Other specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Balance about 20% of Q1 revenue; customised products built around specific customer needs.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

segments.name: Mahad plant
segments.commentary: About 19,900 tpa capacity; utilisation rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26, and management says it was EBITDA and PBT positive in Q1 (about 60% utilisation cited).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR240-250 crores, excluding price fluctuation from geopolitical supply issues and forex gains/losses.
Year-end FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16%.
Normalised gross margin expected at about 30-32%, supported by mix, debottlenecking and captive intermediate consumption.
Management expects pricing to normalise from Q1 elevated levels, with margins moving toward a more sustainable range.
Five-year aspiration of INR2,800-3,000 crores revenue.
Lubricant additive debottlenecking expected to lift capacity 50-70% within 2-3 months; antibacterial product mechanical completion around January, with commercial ramp in the coming year.
Mahad utilisation targeted at 70%-plus by year-end.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity about 98,000 tpa across Khopoli (about 78,800 tpa, near optimum utilisation in FY26) and Mahad (about 19,900 tpa).

Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores over about two years for existing products, including INR50-60 crores for land and infrastructure; expected peak revenue of INR500-550 crores. Funded by internal accruals and possibly more debt.
Phase 1 adds about 60,000 tpa; 10-14 projects to come over the next 12-18 months, with the antibacterial product due in about 6 months and lubricant volume expansion before March.
Phase 2 of INR250-300 crores for new R&D products with better margins; site, product and regulatory work still in progress.
INR25 crores floating-roof acetone storage tank planned, plus more than INR25 crores in the next year for adjoining Khopoli land.
Application testing lab and additional 4,000 sq ft R&D space being built, with investments of about INR15-20 crores for application lab.
demand_pricing: Management says volume grew in the mid-single-digit range in Q1, with demand strong across sectors.
Q1 realisations were lifted by a sharp rise in acetone and petrochemical prices after the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption; the company says it does not speculate on raw materials.
Largest customer is about INR55-60 crores of revenue, against the FY27 revenue target; top 10% of customers are about 24-25% of turnover; more than 1,600 customers.
Management says export volumes to Europe were rising to offset weaker shipments to Africa and the Middle East, and that the West Asia war cost up to about 10% of potential export growth.
Antibacterial product: new technology cuts steps from 10 to 3-3.5; management expects more than 100 tons a month once samples are approved (NDA signed with MNC).
REACH registration for six or seven products; mining chemicals approved in US, with commercial volumes expected in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Phase 1 capacity additions (about 60,000 tpa) mainly extensions of existing products, and is the approach application-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it builds new streams once existing capacity reaches 75-85% utilisation and customer visibility is 3-4 years; it has 10 streams for one client and five hydrogenation reactors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acetone sourcing diversification need storage or logistics investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR25 crores is set aside for a floating-roof storage tank and more than INR25 crores will go into adjoining Khopoli land over the next year, with barge-based shipping expected to cut transport costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance (INR240-250 crores) only modestly above the Q1 run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance excludes about INR25 crores of inventory and forex gains, and it is deliberately conservative given geopolitical uncertainty; it expects Q2 to be near complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Mahad outlook and how much EBITDA did it contribute in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahad is PBT and EBITDA positive; the exact EBITDA number was not given and will be revert-back. Utilisation is about 60%-plus, targeted at 70%-plus by year-end; the extra 20 acres will share overheads.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory higher at quarter-end and how is it managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stock is built from January-February for the April season, with raw materials bought at pre-war prices, and that it does not speculate on raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for additional capex for the R&D pipeline, and on what land?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% of about 40 pipeline products typically get commercialised; the newer chemistry will use the land already bought, and environmental clearance for one or two products is in an advanced stage (9-12 months typical).
